description: Backend event storage + write path + retention. Migration 018 creates the heartbeat_events hypertable and adds heartbeats.history_retention_days; the Timescale store gains the HeartbeatEvent type, the HeartbeatEventWriter interface, and WriteHeartbeatEvent/QueryHeartbeatEvents/CountHeartbeatEventsByType; the ping handler and sweep evaluator write events through a nilable trailing-param writer seam; per-heartbeat retention is threaded through DTO/validator/sqlc/response; the production writer is wired in main.go/router.go; and the retention sweep prunes heartbeat_events. This is a cohesive, buildable backend write-and-prune path. Independent of FEAT-003 (frontend); FEAT-002 (read endpoint) depends on this feature's store methods and Deps wiring.
steps: Create backend/migrations/018_heartbeat_events.up.sql: CREATE TABLE heartbeat_events (id UUID NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), heartbeat_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES heartbeats(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, event_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (event_type IN ('success','fail','missed')), previous_state TEXT CHECK (previous_state IN ('up','down','paused','new')), created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), PRIMARY KEY (id, occurred_at)); CREATE INDEX idx_heartbeat_events_hb_id_occurred_at ON heartbeat_events (heartbeat_id, occurred_at DESC); add a comment that the timescaledb extension is created in migration 004 and intentionally NOT repeated; SELECT create_hypertable('heartbeat_events','occurred_at', if_not_exists => TRUE); then ALTER TABLE heartbeats ADD COLUMN history_retention_days INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 30 CONSTRAINT chk_heartbeat_retention_range CHECK (history_retention_days >= 1 AND history_retention_days <= 365).
Create backend/migrations/018_heartbeat_events.down.sql: ALTER TABLE heartbeats DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS history_retention_days; then DROP TABLE IF EXISTS heartbeat_events;.

In backend/internal/store/timescale/store.go add: type HeartbeatEvent struct { HeartbeatID uuid.UUID; EventType string; PreviousState *string; OccurredAt time.Time }; type HeartbeatEventWriter interface { WriteHeartbeatEvent(ctx context.Context, ev HeartbeatEvent) error }; method (s *Store) WriteHeartbeatEvent — single parameterized INSERT INTO heartbeat_events (heartbeat_id, occurred_at, event_type, previous_state) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4); method (s *Store) QueryHeartbeatEvents(ctx, heartbeatID uuid.UUID, start, end time.Time) ([]HeartbeatEvent, error) — SELECT heartbeat_id, event_type, previous_state, occurred_at WHERE heartbeat_id=$1 AND occurred_at >= $2 AND occurred_at < $3 ORDER BY occurred_at ASC, slice init make([]HeartbeatEvent, 0); method (s *Store) CountHeartbeatEventsByType(ctx, heartbeatID uuid.UUID, start, end time.Time) (map[string]int64, error) — SELECT event_type, COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY event_type. Follow the exact error-wrap/rows.Close/rows.Err idioms used by WriteCheckResult/QueryHistory. Do NOT add a time_bucket method.

In backend/internal/api/handlers/ping.go: add field `events timescale.HeartbeatEventWriter` to PingHandler; change NewPingHandler to accept it as a NEW TRAILING positional parameter (nil valid); add func eventTypeForState(state string) string mapping up->success, down->fail, default logs and returns fail (never missed); add private writeEvent(ctx, id uuid.UUID, eventType, prev string) that returns early on nil writer, sets prevPtr only when prev != "", uses OccurredAt: time.Now().UTC(), and logs on error without failing the ping; call h.writeEvent(c.Request.Context(), row.ID, eventTypeForState(newState), previousState) as the FIRST line of afterTransition. Do NOT write a second event inside Fail. Also update markUpRowToHeartbeat and markFailRowToHeartbeat to copy the new HistoryRetentionDays field (added by sqlc regen in a later step of this feature).

Update the single NewPingHandler call in backend/internal/api/handlers/ping_test.go (around line 40) to pass the new trailing arg; add a recording fake HeartbeatEventWriter and new tests: Success writes event_type success with previous_state; Fail writes fail; nil writer is a no-op; a writer that returns an error is swallowed and the ping still returns 200.

In backend/internal/heartbeat/evaluator.go: add field `events timescale.HeartbeatEventWriter` to Evaluator; change NewEvaluator to accept it as a NEW TRAILING positional parameter (nil valid); in markDown, after a successful MarkHeartbeatDown and alongside the metric/broadcast/dispatch block, guarded by if e.events != nil, write exactly one event timescale.HeartbeatEvent{HeartbeatID: updated.ID, EventType: "missed", PreviousState: &previousState, OccurredAt: time.Now().UTC()}, logging on error. previousState is the locally captured row.State (always "up").

Update the three NewEvaluator calls in backend/internal/heartbeat/evaluator_test.go (around lines 150, 202, 243) to pass the new trailing arg; add a recording fake writer and a test asserting exactly one missed event when MarkHeartbeatDown updates a row and zero events when the guard matches no row (already-down).

Thread retention through the API: in backend/internal/api/handlers/heartbeats.go add HistoryRetentionDays *int32 `json:"history_retention_days,omitempty"` to createHeartbeatRequest ONLY (putHeartbeatRequest is a type alias and inherits it); add validateHeartbeatRetentionDays(days *int32) (int32, error) (nil->30, else must be in [1,365]); invoke it in Create and Put immediately after validateHeartbeatFields and its verr check, returning apiError(c, http.StatusBadRequest, "INVALID_RETENTION_PERIOD", rerr.Error()) on error; pass the validated value into db.CreateHeartbeatParams{...HistoryRetentionDays: retentionDays} and db.UpsertHeartbeatParams{...HistoryRetentionDays: retentionDays}; add HistoryRetentionDays int32 `json:"history_retention_days"` to heartbeatResponse and set it in toHeartbeatResponse from hb.HistoryRetentionDays.

Edit backend/internal/store/postgres/queries/heartbeats.sql: add history_retention_days to CreateHeartbeat (INSERT column list + positional value) and to UpsertHeartbeat (INSERT column list + value AND the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET history_retention_days = EXCLUDED.history_retention_days). Then run `cd backend && sqlc generate`; never hand-edit backend/internal/store/postgres/heartbeats.sql.go.

In backend/internal/retention/service.go add deleteExpiredHeartbeatEvents(ctx, hb db.Heartbeat) (int64, error) using raw s.pool.Exec DELETE FROM heartbeat_events WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM heartbeat_events WHERE heartbeat_id=$1 AND occurred_at<$2 LIMIT $3) with cutoff = now - hb.HistoryRetentionDays*24h and s.deleteLimit; in runCycle, after the monitor loop, add a STRUCTURAL COPY of that loop paging ListHeartbeats via db.ListHeartbeatsParams{Limit: int32(s.batchSize), Offset: offset}: same len(page) < s.batchSize termination, same maxConsecutiveBatchErrors=3 tolerance, same per-item log-and-continue isolation, incrementing the shared s.rowsDeleted counter.

Wire production: in backend/internal/api/router.go add field HeartbeatEventWriter timescale.HeartbeatEventWriter to Deps and append deps.HeartbeatEventWriter to the handlers.NewPingHandler(...) call; in backend/cmd/pulse/main.go set HeartbeatEventWriter: timescaleStore in the api.Deps{...} literal and append timescaleStore to the heartbeat.NewEvaluator(...) call.

Add DB-gated tests in backend/internal/store/timescale/store_test.go (same PULSE_RUN_DB_TESTS gating as existing tests): WriteHeartbeatEvent then QueryHeartbeatEvents round-trips rows in-window ascending respecting [start,end); CountHeartbeatEventsByType returns correct per-type counts; retention pruning removes events older than history_retention_days while in-window rows remain.
acceptance_criteria: `cd backend && go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/pulse` succeeds (migrations embed and compile; *timescale.Store satisfies timescale.HeartbeatEventWriter).
`cd backend && sqlc generate && sqlc diff` reports no drift after adding history_retention_days to the two queries.

`cd backend && go test -race -count=1 ./...` passes, including new ping-handler, evaluator, and retention tests. Unit tests prove: eventTypeForState maps up->success/down->fail; the ping write happens once via afterTransition for both success and fail; nil writer is a no-op and a writer error still yields HTTP 200; the sweep writes exactly one missed event on an up->down transition and none when already down.
DB-gated timescale tests pass under PULSE_RUN_DB_TESTS=1 when Postgres is reachable; when it is not, they are skipped and that is stated (never claimed as passed).
verification: cd backend && sqlc generate && sqlc diff

pg_isready -h localhost -p 5432 -t 3 && cd backend && PULSE_RUN_DB_TESTS=1 go test ./internal/store/timescale/... (ONLY if preflight succeeds; otherwise run without the flag so tests skip and record that integration tests were skipped)
findings:
FEAT-001 complete. Handoff for FEAT-002 (read endpoint) and FEAT-003 (frontend):

STORE API (backend/internal/store/timescale/store.go):
- type HeartbeatEvent struct { HeartbeatID uuid.UUID; EventType string; PreviousState *string; OccurredAt time.Time }. NOTE field order: HeartbeatID, EventType, PreviousState, OccurredAt. QueryHeartbeatEvents SELECTs heartbeat_id, event_type, previous_state, occurred_at (previous_state scanned into *string, so it is nil for NULL).
- interface timescale.HeartbeatEventWriter { WriteHeartbeatEvent(ctx, HeartbeatEvent) error } — declared in the timescale package (not handlers/heartbeat) to avoid an import cycle; *timescale.Store implements it.
- (s *Store) WriteHeartbeatEvent(ctx, ev HeartbeatEvent) error
- (s *Store) QueryHeartbeatEvents(ctx, heartbeatID uuid.UUID, start, end time.Time) ([]HeartbeatEvent, error) — [start,end), ascending by occurred_at, make([]HeartbeatEvent,0).
- (s *Store) CountHeartbeatEventsByType(ctx, heartbeatID uuid.UUID, start, end time.Time) (map[string]int64, error) — keys are event_type values ('success'|'fail'|'missed'); missing types are absent from the map (read with counts["missed"], zero value 0). No time_bucket method (deliberate per design §2.1).

Deps WIRING (backend/internal/api/router.go): api.Deps has a NEW field `HeartbeatEventWriter timescale.HeartbeatEventWriter` (set to timescaleStore in main.go). The TimescaleStore field (*timescale.Store) already exists on Deps and is what FEAT-002's HeartbeatHistoryHandler should use for QueryHeartbeatEvents/CountHeartbeatEventsByType; register the history handler gated on deps.TimescaleStore != nil, like NewHistoryHandler. For FEAT-002, add the handler registration right after heartbeatHandler.Register(protected) in router.go.

SQLC-GENERATED FIELD NAME: db.Heartbeat (and MarkHeartbeatUpRow/MarkHeartbeatFailRow and all SELECT */RETURNING * projections) now carry `HistoryRetentionDays int32` (db/json tag history_retention_days). It is the LAST struct field. In the generated Scan order it is column index 13 (0-based) for plain Heartbeat rows; for MarkHeartbeatUpRow/MarkHeartbeatFailRow the order is ...UpdatedAt(12), HistoryRetentionDays(13), PreviousState(14). CreateHeartbeatParams/UpsertHeartbeatParams gained HistoryRetentionDays int32 — any new CreateHeartbeat call MUST pass a value in [1,365] (DB CHECK chk_heartbeat_retention_range rejects 0; the zero value violates it).

API (backend/internal/api/handlers/heartbeats.go): createHeartbeatRequest (putHeartbeatRequest is a type alias, inherits it) has `HistoryRetentionDays *int32 json:"history_retention_days,omitempty"`. validateHeartbeatRetentionDays(*int32)(int32,error): nil->30, else must be [1,365]. Create/Put return apiError 400 INVALID_RETENTION_PERIOD on out-of-range. heartbeatResponse has `HistoryRetentionDays int32 json:"history_retention_days"`; toHeartbeatResponse copies hb.HistoryRetentionDays. Frontend (FEAT-003) should add history_retention_days:number to the Heartbeat type and CreateHeartbeatRequest.

EVENT SEMANTICS for the timeline (FEAT-002/003): event_type is one of success|fail|missed. up->success, down->fail are the ping-path mappings (handlers.eventTypeForState, single source). 'missed' is written ONLY by the evaluator sweep (one per up->down missed-run episode, previous_state always 'up'). previous_state is populated from the atomically-read prior state (nullable). The invariant success_count+fail_count+missed_count == total_events holds (event_type CHECK). uptime_percent per design §4.3 = success_count/total_events*100 (null when total_events==0).

OPENAPI/DOCS co-change: backend/api/openapi.yaml, docs/API.md, and AGENTS.md were updated in this commit for the retention property + INVALID_RETENTION_PERIOD only (NOT the read endpoint). FEAT-002 must add the GET /heartbeats/{id}/history path + HeartbeatHistoryResponse/HeartbeatEvent/HeartbeatHistorySummary schemas to openapi.yaml in its own commit.

MIGRATION: 018_heartbeat_events (up+down) creates the heartbeat_events hypertable (PK (id, occurred_at), index on (heartbeat_id, occurred_at DESC), ON DELETE CASCADE to heartbeats) and adds heartbeats.history_retention_days. heartbeat_events is NOT sqlc-managed — access only via the timescale store (raw pgx).

TEST-FAKE SURPRISE (for anyone touching these): adding history_retention_days shifted the generated Scan column count. backend/internal/api/handlers/heartbeats_test.go scanHeartbeat now sets dest[13]; markUpRow/markFailRow use dest[:14] + prev at dest[14]. backend/internal/retention/service_test.go TestRunCycle_ConsecutiveBatchErrorsAbort now distinguishes ListMonitors vs ListHeartbeats (two independent loops, each with its own maxConsecutiveBatchErrors=3 budget). createHeartbeat helpers in evaluator_test.go and heartbeats_integration_test.go now pass HistoryRetentionDays:30.

VERIFICATION RESULTS: `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/pulse` OK; `sqlc generate && sqlc diff` clean; `go test -race -count=1 ./...` passes. DB-gated tests ran (Postgres reachable on :5432 via `nc -z -w3`; pg_isready is not installed on this macOS host): `PULSE_RUN_DB_TESTS=1 go test ./internal/store/timescale/... ./internal/heartbeat/... ./internal/store/postgres/...` all pass, including the new heartbeat_events round-trip, CountHeartbeatEventsByType, and retention-pruning tests.
